chunk_text: The deepest exaltation degrees are respectively 10, 3, 28, 15, 5, 27 and 20 for the Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn in their exaltation signs. In the seventh sign from the said exaltation sign, each planet has its own debilitation. The same degrees of deep exaltation apply to deep fall.

chunk_text: In Leo, the first 20 degrees are the Sun's Moolatrikona, while the rest is his own house. For Mars, the first 12 degrees in Aries are Moolatrikona, with the rest being his own house. For Mercury in Virgo, the first 15 degrees are his exaltation zone, the next 5 degrees are Moolatrikona, and the last 10 degrees are his own house. The first one-third of Sagittarius (0-10 degrees) is the Moolatrikona of Jupiter, while the remaining part is his own house. Venus divides Libra into two halves, with the first half (0-15 degrees) as Moolatrikona and the second as own house. Saturn's arrangement in Aquarius is the same as the Sun's in Leo (first 20 degrees are Moolatrikona).
meta_source_ref: BPHS1, Chapter 1 - PLANETARY CHARACTERS AND DESCRIPTION (Part 4)

chunk_text: To determine natural relationships, note the signs which are the 2nd, 4th, 5th, 8th, 9th, and 12th from the Moolatrikona of a planet. The planets ruling these signs are its friends. The lord of its exaltation sign is also a friend. Lords other than these are its enemies. If a planet qualifies as both a friend and an enemy, it becomes neutral.

chunk_text: The natural relationships are as follows: For the Sun, friends are Moon, Mars, Jupiter; enemies are Venus, Saturn; and Mercury is neutral. For the Moon, friends are Sun, Mercury; it has no enemies; and Mars, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn are neutral. For Mars, friends are Sun, Moon, Jupiter; Mercury is the enemy; and Venus, Saturn are neutral. For Mercury, friends are Sun, Venus; the Moon is the enemy; and Mars, Jupiter, Saturn are neutral. For Jupiter, friends are Sun, Moon, Mars; enemies are Mercury, Venus; and Saturn is neutral. For Venus, friends are Mercury, Saturn; enemies are Sun, Moon; and Mars, Jupiter are neutral. For Saturn, friends are Mercury, Venus; enemies are Sun, Moon, Mars; and Jupiter is neutral.

chunk_text: For Rahu: The Sun, Moon and Mars are his enemies. Jupiter, Venus and Saturn are his friends. Mercury is his neutral. For Ketu: The luminaries (Sun and Moon) are his enemies. Mars, Venus and Saturn are his friends, while Mercury and Jupiter are his neutrals.
meta_source_ref: BPHS1, Chapter 1 - PLANETARY CHARACTERS AND DESCRIPTION (Part 4)

chunk_text: The planet posited in the 10th, 4th, 11th, 3rd, 2nd or the 12th house from another becomes a mutual temporary friend. There is temporary enmity otherwise.

chunk_text: Should two planets be naturally and temporarily friendly, they become extremely friendly. Friendship on one count and neutrality on another count make them friendly. Enmity on one count combined with friendship on the other turns into neutrality. Enmity and neutralship cause only enmity. Should there be enmity in both manners, extreme enmity is obtained.

chunk_text: A planet in exaltation gives fully good effects (100%). In Moolatrikona, its auspicious effects are reduced by one fourth (giving 75%). It is half beneficial (50%) in its own house. Its beneficence is one fourth (25%) in a friendly sign. In a neutral's sign, one eighth (12.5%) of its auspicious disposition is useful. The good effects are nil (0%) in debilitation or an enemy's camp. Inauspicious effects are the reverse of what is stated.

chunk_text: To calculate the non-luminous sub-planets (Upagrahas): Add 4 signs 13 degrees and 20 minutes of arc to the Sun's longitude to get the position of the all-inauspicious Dhooma. Reduce Dhooma from 12 signs to arrive at Vyatipata. Add six signs to Vyatipata to know the position of Parivesha. Deduct Parivesha from 12 signs to arrive at the position of Chapa (Indra Dhanus). Add 16 degrees 40 minutes to Chapa to get Upaketu. These are planets devoid of splendour which are malefics by nature and cause affliction.
